# bugs #3435: mcs51: a write through a __data pointer with the constant value 0xB0 does not reach P3

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3435/
- Category: [No action recommended](../../no-action.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Close, as the reporter asks in the last comment. Consider a warning for constants above 0x7F cast to __data pointers.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The case of the ticket's first attachment behaves on r17176 as reported.
`*(__data unsigned char *) 0xB0 = 0xBB;` compiles to `mov r0,#0xb0` and `mov @r0,#0xbb` without a
diagnostic. In ucsim the write changes byte 0xB0 of the internal RAM and leaves P3 unchanged, and
the read through the same pointer returns the RAM byte. The small model, the large model, and the
large model with `--stack-auto` give this result. It is correct, because 0xB0 is not an address in
`__data`.

## Reason

The manual section "__data / __near" defines `__data` as the directly addressable part of the
internal RAM, and "Notes on MCS51 memory layout" gives that RAM as bytes 0x00 to 0x7F. "__idata"
says that the first 128 bytes of `__idata` are the same RAM. "__sfr / __sfr16 / __sfr32 / __sbit"
makes the special function registers an address space of their own. Direct and indirect addressing
reach the same byte for each address in `__data`, so SDCC may dereference `__data` pointers through
`@r0` or `@r1`. The test confirmed this for the address 0x7F. For 0xB0, C11 6.3.2.3 paragraph 5
makes the result of the conversion from an integer to a pointer implementation-defined.

Trunk has changed in three places that the ticket's comments discuss.

- [r14982](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/14982/) added warning 298 for `__data __at`
  declarations whose address is above 0x7F on mcs51. `__data __at (0xB0) TPORT3 PORT3;` from the
  second attachment gets this warning.
- On r17176 `PORT3.U = 0xBB` and `PORT3.B.PIN4 = 1` both use direct addressing, as
  `mov _PORT3,#0xbb` and `orl _PORT3,#0x10`. The assertion on P3 after `PORT3.B.PIN4 = 1`, which
  the second attachment marks as failing, therefore passes. The revision that changed the
  bit-field access was not identified, and the `register __at (0xB0)` variable of that attachment
  was not tested.
- [r13530](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/13530/) changed the casts in `device/lib/_setjmp.c`
  from `__data` to `__idata`, which the twelfth comment announces.

In comments 1 and 4 a maintainer offers a diagnostic for constants above 0x7F that are cast to
`__data` pointers. Trunk does not have it, and it cannot cover pointer values that are unknown at
compile time. A function that dereferences a `__data` pointer parameter compiles to an access
through `@r1`.
